item.title: Fyn Kinase: A Central Regulator in Brain Function, Neurodegeneration, and Cancer
item.description: 🔬 Introduction Fyn kinase is a non-receptor tyrosine kinase belonging to the Src family and plays a critical role in the central nervous system (CNS). It regulates brain development, synaptic signaling, and is strongly implicated in neurodegenerative diseases and cancer. 🧩 Role in Brain Development and Function 🧠 CNS Myelination Fyn is essential for myelination. Loss of Fyn leads to significant myelin deficits in the forebrain. 🔗 Oligodendrocyte Differentiation Fyn interacts with α-tubulin and Tau to stabilize microtubules, enabling oligodendrocytes to form myelin sheaths.

item.title: Electrophysiology (in vivo)
item.description: In vivo electrophysiology is the technique of recording electrical signals from living cells (usually neurons) inside a living animal, such as mouse, rat, or zebrafish. Neurons communicate via electrical signals: Action potentials (spikes) — fast, around 1 ms Local field potentials (LFP) — slower population signals Recording is done as voltage versus time and can be obtained from single neurons or groups of neurons.
